subject: zoology_2
question_text: Name two cranial sutures and their locations.

verification.note: Sourced from 'My Baby Bullet-Q — Senior Inter Zoology' (Star-Q Pass Track Series, Sri Publishers, 2022), book p.50, VSAQ 80. The printed exam years are the book's claim, reproduced here as appearances. Zoology-II holds only ONE source book in the corpus, so the two-book union check is structurally impossible for this card; 'not checked' does NOT mean 'checked and clean'. The mark split is our reading of the question and is a claim until a Telangana IPE teacher confirms it. Text revision (examiner audit, 2026-09-05): the insider note no longer claims a suture is named by the two bones it joins, which the card's own notes on coronal and lambdoid contradict.

page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: Coronal suture
steps.why: A suture is an immovable joint, so naming it means naming the two skull bones locked together there.
common_mistakes: Naming the suture without its location.
Calling a suture a movable joint. Sutures are fixed.
steps.memory_tip: Coronal is like a crown across the front of the head.
steps.margin_note: One line each, with the bones named.
lines: The coronal suture lies between the
frontal bone and the parietal bones.

steps.label: Lambdoid suture
steps.why: It is named for the Greek letter lambda, whose shape it makes at the back of the skull.
common_mistakes: Placing the lambdoid suture at the front. It is at the back.
Giving only one suture when two are asked.
steps.memory_tip: Lambdoid is at the back, shaped like the letter lambda.
steps.margin_note: The second line completes the answer.

insider_note: Neither suture is named after the bones it joins, so the complete answer follows every name with the two bones it lies between.
